note: Per-population rights statements for The Zybach Collection. The material here was made at different times, under different agreements, by different people, for different institutions, so there is no single collection-level statement and no collection-level licence. Each group carries its own. Values are drawn from the RightsStatements.org vocabulary and are limited to InC, UND and InC-RUU. InC-EDU is never used: it asserts an authority to permit third-party educational use that the Library does not hold. No Creative Commons licence is applied to any source material, because a CC grant is irrevocable and the Library cannot give away rights that are not its own.

populations.label: The fifteen printed monographs
populations.gloss: Nobody's ownership of these printed volumes is documented, so the Library says so rather than guessing.
populations.detail: The volumes carry no copyright notice of any kind. That absence does not put them in the public domain — the rule that made a missing notice fatal reaches only works published before 1 March 1989, and every volume here is later. What the missing notice tells us is that ownership was never settled at the time. The title pages recite that the project was authorized and directed by the Director of the OSU Research Forests and funded by the OSU College of Forestry, but a funding recital is not an assignment.

populations.label: Soap Creek interviews recorded 1978–1980
populations.gloss: These interviews were recorded by Royal G. Jackson, Jennifer Lee and Karen Thomas, and the consents ran to the Horner Museum and to Jackson and Lee personally — not to this Library and not to Oregon State.
populations.detail: The 1979 release grants permission to the Horner Museum and to Royal Jackson and Jennifer Lee by name. The 1989 Horner Museum gift and release relinquishes literary rights and legal title to the Horner Museum. The Horner Museum closed in 1995 and its collections went to the Benton County Historical Society in Philomath. Which narrator signed which form is not established: the signed originals are at Oregon State and have not been digitized. We have asked for them.

populations.label: Soap Creek interviews recorded 1989–1991
populations.gloss: The narrators gave their literary rights to Oregon State University's Research Forests, so Oregon State is the door to knock on — not the interviewer and not this Library.
populations.detail: The 1990 OSU Research Forests gift and release is the governing form for this range: "I understand that I am giving away any literary rights or legal titles which I may possess to this gift." It kept two things back for the narrator — personal use, and a checkbox recording whether the narrator was willing to have copies of the transcript distributed to the general public. Where a narrator recorded a choice about public distribution, that choice governs. Which narrator signed which form is not yet established.

populations.label: The 1998-form interview series
populations.statement: In Copyright, with a royalty disclosure
populations.gloss: A different form, limited to educational and research use, and carrying a payment obligation to a county museum that nobody can sign away.
populations.detail: The 1998 form gives permission to reproduce the memoirs for educational and research purposes, and attaches a condition: if content or reproductions are sold, an accurate accounting of total sales is to be made annually and ten per cent of all gross income paid to the Benton County Historical Museum in Philomath, Oregon. The Library discloses that obligation because it survives whatever anyone else signs afterwards, and because anyone contemplating commercial use of this material needs to know about it.
populations.disclosure: Ten per cent of gross income from any sale of this material, and an annual accounting, are owed to the Benton County Historical Museum in Philomath, Oregon. The permission itself is limited to educational and research purposes.

populations.label: Monographs whose printed lead is not the creator

populations.detail: Monographs #02, #04, #13 and #15 were led by Royal G. Jackson with Jennifer Lee or Karen Thomas, and rest on interviews recorded 1978–1980 under the Horner Museum forms. populations.label: Elliott State Forest transcripts
populations.gloss: This is the least settled part of the collection: no signed release has been found for any of these interviews, and several of the narrators are living.
populations.detail: The creator has published these transcripts openly on his own site since 2019, with no rights language attached, and copies are at Oregon State under OH 047. A blank release form exists in the project's files, which suggests the intention was there, but a blank form is not evidence that any were signed. The Library publishes under a considered fair-use rationale with a documented search recorded for each narrator, and treats a narrator's or family's objection as dispositive.

derived.label: The layer the Library built
derived.statement: The Library's own work. Licence terms to be announced.
derived.gloss: The indexes, place and people pages, the timeline, the finding aid and the page anchoring are the Library's work, not the creator's, and the Library says so.
derived.detail: An open licence is under consideration for this layer and has not been granted. When the Library decides, it will say so here and date the decision. Whatever it decides covers only the layer the Library made: it does not, and cannot, cover the underlying sources, because the Library cannot give away rights that are not its own. Parts of this layer are built from material that carries a use limitation — the 1998-form series is limited to educational and research purposes and carries a royalty — and any licence must keep those parts separable.
